questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield just to the traffic on the right.
Yield just to the traffic on the left.
Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.
questions.explanation: A yield sign tells you to slow down and let other traffic go first before you enter the intersection or roadway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A yellow triangular sign with black lettering means no passing is allowed. It appears on the left side of two-lane roads where there are also road markings showing no passing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that an intersection is coming so you can prepare to turn or watch for traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Construction workers on or near the roadway.

questions.explanation: Yellow diamond-shaped warning signs with black markings alert drivers to hazards. This sign warns that pedestrians may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must go straight ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a road is coming in from the right side ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep or long downgrade is ahead. The hill may have sharp curves, so be prepared.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs mean you must stop and yield the right-of-way at an intersection. You can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Lane reduction; the right lane ends soon.
Lane reduction; the left lane ends soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane reduction; the right lane ends soon.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane will end soon.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Mileage information, such as distances to specific locations.

questions.explanation: Blue signs provide information about services available nearby, such as rest areas, food, gas, or hospitals.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Last turn before a toll road.

questions.explanation: Orange signs mark work zones. This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. You must follow the flagger's directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.explanation: A green arrow pointing down means you can use that lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles like farm tractors and road maintenance equipment display an orange and red triangle on the back.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill grade is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A round sign always means a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Bicyclists use hand and arm signals instead of turn signals. A left arm straight out signals a left turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you to drive carefully because the road may become wet and slippery.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are permitted on an upcoming narrow bridge.
The bridge ahead is open to one-way traffic only.
The bridge ahead is wide enough for only one car at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you the upcoming bridge may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck. Drive carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that a divided highway is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.explanation: This sign forbids right turns. You cannot turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign shows a pedestrian crosswalk. Be alert and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: May pass a slow-moving vehicle if you can do so quickly.
May pass if you know the road ahead.
May pass, but only at night.

questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It is white and rectangular with black markings. You must follow the instructions on all regulatory signs. This sign means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: The stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on the road. When you see a stop sign, you must come to a complete stop. Do not proceed until it is safe and clear to pass through the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a T intersection is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that a T intersection is coming. Be ready to turn right or left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign alerts you to an immediate hazard ahead. It tells you that traffic will merge from the right side. Be prepared to allow that traffic to merge safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Be ready to merge with traffic entering your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to merge with traffic entering your lane.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that traffic will merge in from the right. Get ready to allow that traffic to merge safely into your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: May either continue through the interchange or exit the freeway from your current lane.
May stay in your lane and continue through the interchange.
Must exit the freeway, if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must exit the freeway, if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means the lane ends and becomes an exit ramp. You cannot stay in that lane through the interchange. You must either change to another lane to continue forward, or you must exit the freeway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Until after you pass the sign.
Unless it seems safe to do so.

questions.explanation: This is a white rectangular sign that shows a rule you must follow. This sign means you cannot pass other vehicles under any circumstances.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: That the right lane ends and traffic should merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the right lane ends and traffic should merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the right lane will end ahead. All traffic in the right lane must move to the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign alerts you that bicycles may cross the road ahead. Be alert and ready to share the road.
